bugs.summary: notion.so - "Reposition" feature for images does not work

comments.author: ctanase@mozilla.com
comments.creator: ctanase@mozilla.com
comments.raw_text:
**Environment:**
Operating system: Linux / Windows 10
Firefox version: Firefox 134.0 (release) / 136

**Preconditions:**
- Account needed (login with Google account available)
- Clean profile

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Navigate to: https://www.notion.so/
2. Log in with your account.
3. Go to an existing page (or create one by clicking on the button "Create a new page" next to your account name).
4. Hover above the page title.
5. Click on "Add cover".
6. Hover over the cover and  click "Reposition".
7. Click and drag down the cover and release.
8. Observe the behavior.

**Expected Behavior:**
The cover position changes and can be saved.

**Actual Behavior:**
The cover position resets and editing mode cancels.

**Notes:**
- Reproducible on the latest Firefox Release and Nightly
- Reproducible regardless of the ETP setting
- Works as expected using Chrome

---

Created from webcompat-user-report:9c0163eb-a3e8-4c23-b759-c25bb1a3cc1a

comments.raw_text:
For reference, the JS in comment 3 is here, for me at least:
https://www.notion.so/_assets/73155-2def67dbe976f2b2.js

I spent a little while poking around to see if I could learn more about why `o(965903).default.state.stores.length` is different when mouseup arrives, but it's non-trivial...  I did find that `o` here seems to be some sort of registry of various objects with numeric IDs, and the `965903` object-id is only passed in a few places. In particular, the places I found were: the spot quoted in comment 3, and here:
```
      z = () => o(965903),
```
https://www.notion.so/_assets/floatingTableOfContents-4211eca2e9c2929d.js
(so in that file, all `z()` usages are referring to this same object with the all-important `default.state.stores.length` value)

...and in a bunch of spots in this file (with different single-character aliases similar to the `z` one above):
https://www.notion.so/_assets/91852-b680287d52efaae9.js

I'm not immediately finding where/why that object's `default.state.stores` array is going from empty to non-empty, though.

comments.raw_text: Sounds like Chrome does not make the editing host get focused when it does not have focus and mouse down on non-editable element. If it's right, I guess [`EventStateManager::PostHandleEvent` sets focus to the editing host](https://searchfox.org/firefox-main/rev/55aaa33f526ad11857e3f2e07a87daef1aa56ad4/dom/events/EventStateManager.cpp#915,4111,4129-4130) and modifying here will fix this bug. Although I don't have much time for now because this is a risky change and may need follow up work for regressions.
